blocks.text: Why supply chain planners need better Slack habits

You juggle ERP dashboards, Excel sheets, and constant Slack notifications. This context switching kills your focus. When you need to find a specific PO number or a shipping update, you often end up scrolling through channels for minutes. The goal is to spend less time managing the app and more time managing the supply chain. Use the built in keyboard shortcuts to stay on your keyboard.

items: Press Command plus / to see the full list of shortcuts inside Slack.
Use Command plus K to open the quick switcher and jump to any conversation.
Press Shift plus Enter to add a line break instead of sending a message.
Use Command plus B or I to format your text quickly for readability.

blocks.text: Use Slack for supply chain planners on Mac more efficiently

Your Mac is a powerful tool, but it can get cluttered. Keep your Slack notifications under control so you only see what matters. If a specific project channel becomes too noisy, right click the channel name and select Mute. You can still check it later, but it will not interrupt your focus while you are deep in a forecast model. Use the Unreads view to catch up on everything at once at the end of the hour.
Search like a pro in Slack

Searching for a file or a message is a daily chore. Do not just type a keyword and hit Enter. Use modifiers to narrow your results. Type from: followed by a colleague name to find messages from your warehouse lead. Use has:file to find those PDFs or invoices that were shared weeks ago. This saves you from digging through file storage systems.

items: Search in current channel with Command plus F.
Use in: to search within a specific channel or DM.
Use before: or after: to filter by date range.
Use has:link to find shared URLs for tracking portals.

blocks.text: Lazur acts as a bridge for your voice. When you are busy, hold the Option and Command keys to ask about something on your screen. If you are looking at a messy Slack thread, ask Lazur to summarize the latest updates. It helps you stay on top of urgent shipment changes without needing to read every single message. When you need to reply, hold the fn key to dictate your response. It will be formatted and ready to send at the cursor.

Sometimes the app slows down or notifications stop appearing. If you notice Slack acting strange, go to the Help menu, select Troubleshooting, and choose Clear Cache and Restart. This fixes most performance issues. If you are not getting alerts, check your system settings. Go to System Settings, then Notifications, and ensure Slack is set to allow alerts. If you still have trouble, you can always check the official Slack help center.

Create a dedicated channel for each supplier or project. This keeps your communication siloed and easy to manage. If a conversation turns into a task, use the save for later feature. Hover over the message, click the three dots, and select Save. You can view all your saved items by clicking the Saved items icon at the top of your sidebar. This creates a personal to do list inside Slack.

faq.question: How can I search for messages from a specific person in Slack?
faq.answer: Type from: followed by the name of the person in the search bar. Slack will filter the results to show only messages sent by them.

faq.question: What is the fastest way to jump to a new channel?
faq.answer: Press Command plus K on your Mac keyboard. This opens the Quick Switcher, where you can type the name of any channel or person to jump there immediately.

faq.question: How do I fix Slack if it feels slow?
faq.answer: Go to the Help menu in the menu bar, select Troubleshooting, and then click Clear Cache and Restart. This refreshes the app and often resolves performance lag.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me write messages in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. You can hold the fn key to dictate your response. Lazur will type the text at your cursor, allowing you to draft messages quickly while keeping your hands on the keyboard.
